history.period: c. 300 years old (idol said to have been discovered ~18th century)
history.summary: Famous Shakti temple at Sigandur village, Kalasavalli (post Tumari, PIN 577453), Sagar taluk, Shivamogga district (CSV town 'Shimoga' corrected: Shimoga is the district headquarters; the temple is at Sigandur, ~35 km from Sagar). Local tradition: the idol was found ~300 years ago on the bank of the Sharavathi river after hunter Sheshappa dreamt of the goddess; he and Brahmin Duggajja built the temple, and their families remain trustee/priest lineages. Devotees regard Chowdeshwari Amma as protector of the innocent and obtain temple boards reading 'Shri deviya rakshane ide' to safeguard land. The temple is effectively an island in the Sharavathi/Linganamakki backwaters and is reached by barge/launch across the water from the Sagar side. Darshan-timing sources conflict (e.g. 5 AM-2:30 PM + 4-7 PM vs 3:30-7 AM, 8 AM-2:30 PM, 5:30-7:30 PM); confirm locally before visiting.

name: Sri Sigandur Chowdeshwari Temple
town_description: Sigandur is a small village in Sagar taluk, Shivamogga district, about 35 km from Sagar town. Surrounded by the backwaters of the Sharavathi river (Linganamakki reservoir), it is known almost entirely for its Chowdeshwari temple, reached by ferry/barge.

travel.airport: Shivamogga (RQY) ~105 km (verify); Mangaluru (IXE) is an alternative coastal option (verify)
travel.railway: Shimoga Town (SMET) ~105 km; Talaguppa/Sagara Jambagaru are the nearest small stations (verify)
travel.road: Reach Sagar (Sagara) first (~105 km from Shivamogga), then ~35 km by bus to Sigandur; final access across the backwaters is by launch/barge, which carries vehicles too

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Tuesdays and Fridays are considered special (verify)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 5:00 AM-2:30 PM and 4:00-7:00 PM (verify - sources conflict; midday break 2:30-4:00 PM)
